summary: Chevening is the UK government's global scholarship for future leaders, funded by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office and partners. It pays for a one-year master's degree at any UK university for citizens of more than 160 countries and territories.
covers: Full tuition fees for an eligible one-year taught master's at any UK university.
A monthly living allowance (stipend) for the year.
Return economy travel to the UK, arrival and departure allowances, and the cost of one visa application.
Access to Chevening's events and alumni network during and after your year.
eligibility: Citizenship of a Chevening-eligible country or territory, and a commitment to return there for at least two years after the award ends.
An undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's.
At least two years (2,800 hours) of work experience gained after your first degree.
Applications to three different eligible UK master's courses, and an unconditional offer from one of them by the July deadline.
how_to_apply: Shortlist three one-year master's courses at UK universities and check they are Chevening-eligible.
Complete the online application, including four essays: leadership, networking, studying in the UK, and your career plan.
Submit between 4 August and 6 October 2026 (11:00 UTC) for 2027–28 study.
If shortlisted, interview at the British embassy or high commission (March–April), then secure an unconditional course offer by early July.
watch_out: The 2027–28 deadline is 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC — earlier than the early-November dates used in some past cycles.
Essays decide who gets an interview. Specific examples of leadership and a concrete post-study plan beat general statements.
Chevening never charges a fee to apply. Beware of social-media pages claiming to 'process' applications — see our [scam guide]({{root}}guides/scholarship-scams/).
